title: Rhoform Bake-off Design Model v0
description:
ARM-NEUTRAL description of one design, used only by the §8-Q1 syntax bake-off (issue AMB-32 / roadmap R5b). It is the thing every candidate grammar and the Starlark baseline must express, so that a token-cost comparison between them is a comparison of GRAMMARS rather than of designs. Each arm renders a model to source and parses source back to a model; the round trip and the cross-arm agreement are what make the numbers comparable.

THIS IS NOT THE IR. ir/netlist-ir.schema.json describes a fully ELABORATED design: flattened nets, resolved parameters, content hashes, generator metadata. This describes SOURCE-LEVEL facts before elaboration: module definitions, their instances, their local nets. The vocabularies that both share — pin roles, hardware kinds, measurement kinds, path-safe identifiers — are deliberately identical, and lang/tests/test_bakeoff.py fails if they ever drift apart.

THIS IS A THROWAWAY FIXTURE FORMAT. R5b's prototypes are explicitly disposable; the frozen grammar's real source of truth lands in AMB-33/R6 and the living benchmark sources in AMB-50/R53. Nothing outside lang/ may depend on this schema.

model_version.description: Integer schema version. Any shape change bumps it. Held at 0 for the whole of M0.

stability.description: Constant, and deliberately not a free field: a bake-off fixture format can never be a contract. A model claiming stability is rejected here rather than in review.

design_id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier for this design, used as the corpus key and in report output, e.g. "blinker-555".

root_module.description: Name of the module definition in `modules` that is the top of this design. Every other module must be reachable from it by instantiation; an unreachable definition is dead weight in a token-cost measurement and is rejected by the loader.

purpose.description: "reference": a transcription of a benchmark design, which MUST declare an anchor — a reference netlist nothing external agrees with is an opinion. "coverage-probe": a synthetic design whose job is to exercise every field of this schema at least once, so that an arm which cannot express something fails the gate instead of waiting for a corpus that happens to hit it. A probe has nothing external to anchor to and must not claim one.
purpose.$comment: The Starlark arm could not express exclude_from_bom on a component without a hardware kind, and the gate passed for months of nothing because neither benchmark used that combination.

source_benchmark.description: Repository-relative directory of the benchmark reference design this model transcribes (authored under AMB-39). Present when the model is a transcription rather than an invention; the loader cross-checks the transcription against that directory's committed artifacts, so a fixture cannot quietly drift from the design it claims to represent.

anchor.description: Optional external artifact this model is checked against. An anchor authored by a DIFFERENT issue is the only defence against a bake-off whose reference was tailored to its own parsers.

modules.description: All module definitions, sorted bytewise-ascending by `name` (the loader enforces the order, so two models describing the same design serialize identically).

assertions.description: Design assertions declared on the root module, sorted bytewise-ascending by `name`. Assertion syntax is part of the surface under test, so the corpus carries real ones.

notes.description: Free-text provenance: where the connectivity came from, what was inferred, what was deliberately left out.

Identifier.description: A DSL identifier. Same production in every arm: identifier spelling is not one of the axes under test, so holding it constant keeps the token comparison honest.

QualifiedName.description: Dotted definition name, matching the IR's `Instance.definition` production exactly, e.g. "rhoform.lib.passive.Resistor".

NetName.description: Explicit net label. The IR permits '.' and '/' in derived net names; a model only ever carries labels a human wrote, which are plain identifiers.

Quantity.description:
A dimensioned literal in the SHARED quantity mini-language. Five forms, all of them T4 value kinds:
  `100kohm`                        exact
  `100kohm +/- 1%`                 symmetric relative tolerance
  `2.0V +/- 0.2V`                  symmetric absolute tolerance
  `9.5mA (8.0mA to 10.5mA)`        nominal with an asymmetric interval
  `3.0V to 3.6V`                   interval with no nominal
Held IDENTICAL across all arms on purpose — T3 fixes literals as value-exact with a canonical SI normal form, so literal spelling is settled by requirement and is not an A/B axis; letting it vary would charge one candidate for a decision that is not its to make. ASCII only (L5): the tolerance sign is `+/-`, never U+00B1. There is no exponent form, so every literal has exactly one spelling. The decimal text is preserved exactly and compared as an exact decimal, never as a float, so 0.1 means 0.1.

Value.description: A parameter or constraint value. Exactly one form, tagged by key: `q` dimensioned quantity, `s` symbolic string, `i` exact integer, `b` flag. Mirrors the IR's ParameterValue oneOf, but tagged rather than inferred from the JSON type — an untagged "0805" and an untagged 805 are one typo apart, and the tag makes that unrepresentable.

s.description: Symbolic value, e.g. a package code. Printable ASCII only (L5).

ValueMap.description: Map from parameter name to value. Key order in the file is irrelevant; the loader sorts.

PinRole.description: T2 pin-role lattice. MUST stay identical member-for-member to ir/netlist-ir.schema.json#/$defs/PinRole — lang/tests/test_bakeoff.py reads both files and fails on any divergence, so the two cannot drift silently the way two hand-maintained enums otherwise do.

HardwareKind.description: L9 fabrication-reality classification. Identical member-for-member to the IR's Instance.hardware_kind enum, checked by the same conformance test as PinRole.

items.description: Physical pin designator on the footprint, e.g. "1", "A3", "EP".

pin_numbers.description: Footprint pins bound to this logical port; several means they are internally common (paired GND pins). Components only — a module port has no physical pin. Sorted by the loader.

PartBinding.description:
Reference-only part binding (D1), matching the IR's discriminated shape. The model never inlines part data.

A RESOLVED part may carry constraints as well as a key — the IR keeps them as the provenance record of what the pick was required to satisfy, so that re-resolution has to be explicit rather than silent. An earlier draft used `oneOf` here and rejected exactly that, which the 555's resolved-with-constraints binding caught.

binding.description: "abstract": only the constraint set is known. "resolved": pinned in the parts lockfile.

constraints.description: Constraint set the part must satisfy.

lockfile_key.description: Opaque stable key into the design's parts lockfile.

InstanceDef.description: One member of a module: either a component leaf or a nested module instantiation.

definition.description: For kind=module, the `name` of another entry in `modules`. For kind=component, the library-qualified component name.

ports.description: Component ports with their T2 roles and footprint pins. Omitted for kind=module: a module instance's interface is its definition's `ports`, and repeating it would let the two disagree.

dnp.description: L9 do-not-populate. Absent means false; the renderer emits the attribute only when true, so the token cost of a flag is the cost of the ones that are actually set.

PortRef.description: A connection endpoint inside a module. `instance.port` names a child's port; a bare identifier names one of THIS module's own declared ports, which is how an internal net reaches the enclosing scope.

NetDef.description:
A net local to one module definition.

A net is an equivalence class of ports, so an UNLABELLED net's identity is exactly its member set — which is why `name` is optional. Modelling every net as labelled would have been simpler and would have quietly rigged the measurement: a two-member link like `ctl ~ r_lim.a` costs one line in a pin-to-pin grammar and three in a label-then-attach grammar, so forcing a label on it charges one candidate for a modelling artifact rather than for its own syntax. Labels appear where a human would write one (rails, named signals) and nowhere else.

What is NOT modelled here is DERIVED naming — the rule that invents a name for an unlabelled net. That is I2's stable-identity problem, and letting each arm apply its own rule would make cross-arm comparison depend on the rule rather than on the syntax.

name.description: Explicit label, when the design gives the net one. Absent means an unlabelled net identified by its members.

members.description: Endpoints joined by this net, sorted by the loader. A single-member net is legal and intentional (L9b): H2-H4 in benchmark (c) exist to exercise exactly that rule.

ground_domain.description: Optional T5 ground-domain label, carried through to the IR's Net.ground_domain.

voltage_domain.description: Optional T5 voltage-domain label, carried through to the IR's Net.voltage_domain.

name.description: Name the DSL source declares and instantiates, unique across `modules`.

qualified_name.description: Fully qualified definition name this module elaborates to in the IR (e.g. "rhoform.lib.display.LedIndicator"). Recorded so a model can be checked against an IR anchor whose `definition` fields are qualified, without putting import syntax — L4's business, not L5's — into the bake-off.

ports.description: This module's own interface. A port here has no `pin_numbers`.

instances.description: Members, sorted bytewise-ascending by `name` by the loader.

nets.description: Local nets, sorted bytewise-ascending by `name` by the loader.

MeasurementKind.description: V2 measurement vocabulary, v1 — CLOSED. Identical member-for-member to the IR's MeasurementKind, checked by the same conformance test as PinRole.

name.description: Assertion name as written in source; becomes the IR assertion's path segment.

subject.description: Net probed by this assertion. The IR's Probe also admits port and instance forms; the bake-off corpus only needs the net form, and admitting forms the corpus never exercises would put untested syntax into every arm's grammar.

bounds.description: Acceptance bounds; at least one of min/max, both means a closed interval. Matches the IR's AssertionBounds.

unit.description: Unit of both bounds; "1" for dimensionless.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound as EXACT DECIMAL TEXT, not a JSON number. A bound of 0.932 Hz that round-trips through an IEEE double is no longer 0.932, and an assertion window is precisely where that must not happen (T3 value-exactness).

max.description: Inclusive upper bound as exact decimal text.

Anchor.description: An external artifact this model is verified against, so the bake-off's reference cannot be quietly reshaped to suit its own parsers.

kind.description: "netlist-ir": the model, elaborated and flattened, must reproduce that IR document's instances, nets, connections and assertions. "parts-yaml": the model's component set must match that BOM's refdes/dnp population exactly.

path.description: Repository-relative path of the anchor artifact.

power_tree.description: For a parts-yaml anchor: the benchmark's power tree, whose declared series edges (`from`/`to` between supply nodes) the flattened netlist must reproduce. A BOM anchors no connectivity at all, so without this the netlist every measurement runs over would be self-certified.

refdes_map.description: For a parts-yaml anchor: map from BOM refdes (e.g. "C12") to this model's instance path (e.g. "/c12"). Explicit rather than derived by lowercasing, so a BOM entry that no instance covers is a hard error instead of a silent near-miss.
